injuries.longComment: Jones is still recovering from right knee surgery she underwent this offseason and remains without a clear timetable for a return. She can be considered doubtful for future contests until the Dream offer an update on her progress.
injuries.shortComment: Jones (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Phoenix.

injuries.longComment: day-to-day
injuries.shortComment: day-to-day

injuries.longComment: Westbeld will sit out Saturday's contest in an effort to preserve her eligibility while signed to a developmental pact. Her next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Tempo.
injuries.shortComment: Westbeld (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Minnesota, Kareem Copeland of ESPN reports.

injuries.longComment: Carrington has yet to make her season debut after undergoing left foot surgery in April. She can be considered doubtful for future games until the Sky offer an update on her progress.
injuries.shortComment: Carrington (foot) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Minnesota.

injuries.longComment: Vandersloot is still recovering from the right knee surgery she underwent last June to repair a torn ACL, and she remains without a clear timetable for a return. The veteran guard can be considered doubtful for future contests until the Sky provide an update on her progress.
injuries.shortComment: Vandersloot (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.
injuries.shortComment: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: Nelson-Ododa is trending toward playing Monday after a four-game absence due to a right ankle injury. Over three regular-season appearances (one start), the 25-year-old center is averaging 6.7 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.0 steals across 16.3 minutes per contest.
injuries.shortComment: Nelson-Ododa (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against the Valkyries.

injuries.longComment: Griner is likely to return from a two-game absence due to a right rib sprain, and her presence would leave fewer minutes available for Raegan Beers. Griner is averaging 15.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.4 combined steals-plus-blocks in 27.3 minutes per game across three regular-season outings.
injuries.shortComment: Griner (rib) is probable for Monday's game against Golden State.

injuries.longComment: This was to be expected, as Lacan is preparing for an international championship series with Basket Landes that could end as late as May 17. With Marina Mabrey gone, Lacan should have a major role when she returns after averaging 11.7 points, 4.7 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 2.1 steals in 30.9 minutes in games she played at least 25 minutes last season (14 times).
injuries.shortComment: Lacan remains overseas, so the Sun temporarily suspended her contract Thursday, Khristina Williams of MSG Network reports.

injuries.longComment: day-to-day
injuries.shortComment: day-to-day

injuries.longComment: Fankam Mendjiadeu, who has yet to log a single minute for the Wings this season, will return to the inactive list Sunday. Her next chance to join the active roster will come Thursday versus the Aces.
injuries.shortComment: Fankam Mendjiadeu (coach's decision) won't play Sunday in New York.

injuries.longComment: Jocyte missed the preseason and the beginning of the regular season due to an overseas commitment. She's missed the last two games for reconditioning purposes but has a chance to make her WNBA debut Monday.
injuries.shortComment: Jocyte (reconditioning) is questionable for Monday's game against the Sun, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Zandalasini is in danger of missing a fifth consecutive contest while in the league's concussion protocol. If the 30-year-old guard isn't cleared to return, Kaitlyn Chen will likely continue seeing increased minutes off the bench.
injuries.shortComment: Zandalasini (concussion) is questionable for Monday's game against the Sun, Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.
injuries.shortComment: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.

injuries.longComment: The Fever are preserving Pissott's availability Friday. The rookie guard is eligible to be active for 12 regular-season games under her developmental deal, and she's still waiting to make her WNBA debut.
injuries.shortComment: Pissott (coach's decision) is out for Friday's game against the Valkyries.

injuries.longComment: Hall will sit out Friday's contest in an effort to preserve her eligibility while signed to a developmental contract. Her next chance to play will come Thursday against Golden State.
injuries.shortComment: Hall (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Valkyries.

injuries.longComment: Evans wasn't included on the Aces' initial injury report, though she'll end up missing a sixth straight regular-season game due to a left leg injury. Her next chance to play will come Thursday in Dallas.
injuries.shortComment: Evans (leg) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Sparks.

injuries.shortComment: day-to-day

injuries.longComment: Ziegler will return to the inactive list to conserve her total games played. Her next chance to suit up will come Friday versus the Mystics.
injuries.shortComment: Ziegler (coach's decision) won't play against the Aces on Saturday.

injuries.longComment: Feagin was available for the Sparks' opener versus the Aces, logging only three minutes. However, since then, she hasn't played and will miss her fifth-consecutive game Saturday, although her absence isn't expected to have much of an impact on the rotation.
injuries.shortComment: Feagin (leg) is listed as out for Saturday's game against the Aces.

injuries.longComment: day-to-day
injuries.shortComment: day-to-day

injuries.longComment: Juhasz is dealing with a right mid-foot sprain, per Borzi, and will miss at least the next five games, including Thursday's clash against Toronto. A more exact timeline for her return should come into focus as she begins to clear hurdles in her rehab.
injuries.shortComment: Juhasz (foot) is expected to remain out for another 2-to-3 weeks, Pat Borzi of MinnPost reports.

injuries.longComment: Cechova suffered a non-contact injury during Thursday's 90-86 win over Dallas and required assistance off the floor. After undergoing an MRI, she was diagnosed with a torn ACL, ending her season. The 21-year-old rookie appeared in three games, and she will finish the 2026 campaign by averaging 8.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 0.3 steals and 0.7 blocks across 17.3 minutes. With Cechova sidelined, Anastasiia Kosu could be first in line to see more action.
injuries.shortComment: Cechova (knee) was diagnosed with a torn ACL in her right knee and will undergo surgery, Meghan L. Hall of USA Today reports. She will miss the remainder of the season.

injuries.longComment: Collier underwent surgery on both of her ankles in early January and will miss time at the beginning of the campaign after having another procedure on her left ankle. The superstar forward signed a one-year, $1.4 million contract with the Lynx on Thursday and is coming off a career-best year in 2025, during which she averaged 22.9 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.6 steals and 1.5 blocks in 32.3 minutes per contest. She also shot 53.1 percent from the field, 40.3 percent from beyond the arc and 90.6 percent from the charity stripe. Her absence will likely result in expanded roles for Courtney Williams, Kayla McBride (ear) and Natasha Howard, while Nia Coffey and Anastasiia Kosu could see increased playing time.
injuries.shortComment: Collier underwent surgery on her left ankle March 24 and is expected to return to on-court activities in early June, Sara Jane Gamelli of BallisLife.com reports.

injuries.longComment: day-to-day
injuries.shortComment: day-to-day

injuries.longComment: Per Myles Ehrlich of Winsidr.com, Fiebich was spotted off to the side at Saturday's practice. Although she will not play Sunday after having her contract temporarily suspended May 7 due to an overseas commitment, the 26-year-old forward could return for the second leg of New York's back-to-back set. Her return would leave fewer minutes available for Pauline Astier and Rebekah Gardner.
injuries.shortComment: Fiebich (overseas commitment) could return as soon as Monday's game against the Fire, Annie Costabile of The Athletic reports.

injuries.longComment: Fauthoux was selected by the Liberty with the No. 29 pick of the 2021 WNBA Draft but has spent the last five seasons overseas. She's joining the team as a developmental player and wants to make her WNBA debut this year. However, Fauthoux continues to recover from ACL surgery, so it's unclear when she would be available to make her league debut.
injuries.shortComment: Fauthoux (knee) will be joining the Liberty for the 2026 season, Myles Ehrlich of Winsidr.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Ciezki will return to the sidelines to conserve her games played count. Her next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against the Liberty.
injuries.shortComment: Ciezki (coach's decision) is out for Sunday's game versus the Dream.

injuries.longComment: Akoa Makani is officially back with the team after fulfilling her overseas obligations, but she's still not quite ready to make her regular-season debut. Her next chance to play will come Wednesday in New York.
injuries.shortComment: Akoa Makani (reconditioning) has been ruled out for Sunday's game in Atlanta.

injuries.longComment: This is a tough blow for Whitcomb and the Mercury as she will now miss the first month or so of the WNBA season. Whitcomb served as a part-time starter during her first season in Phoenix last year, averaging 9.1 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 23.9 minutes per game across 43 regular-season appearances (20 starts). Kiana Williams could see an uptick in minutes with this news.
injuries.shortComment: Whitcomb will undergo an arthroscopy on Thursday to remove a loose body in her left knee. She will be re-evaluated in four to six weeks, Shane Young of the Mercury's official site reports.

injuries.longComment: This will be Malonga's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list, and it's not encouraging that she continues to get ruled out a full day before tipoff. For now, she should be considered questionable at best for Wednesday's rematch with the Mystics.
injuries.shortComment: Malonga (concussion) won't play Sunday against the Mystics.

injuries.longComment: Magbegor sustained her injury while playing for Australia in the 2026 FIBA Basketball World Cup Qualifiers, and she appears to be on track to miss the start of the WNBA regular season as a result. The 26-year-old has played a prominent role in Seattle's frontcourt across the past several seasons, most recently averaging 8.0 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.2 blocks and 2.1 assists in 27.3 minutes per game while starting every regular-season matchup in 2025, while her absence to begin the 2026 season could lead to increased opportunities for Dominique Malonga, Stefanie Dolson and rookie Awa Fam.
injuries.shortComment: The Storm announced Monday that Magbegor is expected to miss at least 6-8 weeks due to a right foot injury, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Harrison will remain on the sidelines for a seventh consecutive game to open the regular season while recovering from a right hand injury sustained during training camp. Head coach Sandy Brondello recently indicated that the veteran forward is targeting a return to action sometime in early June, meaning a definitive timeline should begin to emerge once she is cleared to ramp up basketball activities
injuries.shortComment: Harrison (hand) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Fire.

injuries.longComment: Allemand will miss a fourth consecutive contest Saturday, though she can be considered day-to-day ahead of Wednesday's game in Chicago. In the meantime, Kiki Rice, Laura Juskaite and Kia Nurse are candidates to see increased burn.
injuries.shortComment: Allemand, who has already been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Fire, is ramping back up after sustaining a Grade 1 groin strain, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet reports.

injuries.longComment: Fagbenle is set to sit out her fifth straight contest Thursday versus Minnesota due to a nagging right shoulder injury. The timeline for a return likely means she'll miss at least three more games after Thursday, keeping Laura Juskaite and Teonni Key in larger roles for the time being.
injuries.shortComment: Fagbenle (shoulder) is unlikely to return before the end of May, per Chelsea Leite of TSN.
